title: Traffic orchestration manifest and safety checklist
content:
Purpose
-----
Working notes for a compact manifest/schema to express traffic orchestration rules that the control plane can validate, compile, and rollout safely across regions. This doc focuses on the schema shape (YAML/JSON), validators to run pre-apply, telemetry gates for canary progression, and a practical rollout checklist for multi-region scenarios.

Audience
--------
Platform engineers, SREs, release engineers, and infra product owners who author or review routing manifests. This is intentionally a working document — expect follow-ups and concrete PRs to land in control-plane.

Design goals / constraints
-------------------------
- Single manifest for a logical routing policy that can target multiple regions and model variants.
- Declarative: the manifest should be fully verifiable by rwctl / control-plane validators before any rollout.
- Fail-safe defaults: any unspecified value should bias towards conservative behaviour (zero traffic, short canaries).
- Observable: every rollout step must map to telemetry and an explicit gating condition.
- Capacity-aware routing: the control plane uses regional capacity signals to scale weights rather than blindly shifting traffic.

High level schema (human-friendly)
----------------------------------
Below is the suggested YAML-authoring surface. The control plane stores canonical JSON but we author in YAML for readability. Keep the manifest small; complex logic should be encoded in named policies referenced by the manifest.

EXAMPLE MANIFEST (YAML)
-----------------------
# name: unique policy id
# target: logical route (e.g., /api/v1/generate)
# selectors: matchers used by gateway/edge to apply policy
# variants: list of model/service variants to route to
# rollout: staged rollout instructions with telemetry gates

name: conversational-model-defaults
target: /api/v1/generate
selectors:
  - path_prefix: /api/v1/generate
  - header: x-tenant-id
variants:
  - id: redwood-llama-7b-qat
    region_policy:
      - region: us-west-2
        max_weight: 0.6
      - region: eu-central-1
        max_weight: 0.4
    runtime_profile: small-latency-50ms
    capacity_hint: tokens_per_minute: 120000
  - id: redwood-llama-7b-quant2
    region_policy:
      - region: us-west-2
        max_weight: 0.4
    runtime_profile: cheap-throughput
    capacity_hint: tokens_per_minute: 300000
rollout:
  strategy: progressive-canary
  initial_step: 1
  steps:
    - name: canary-1
      percent: 1
      duration: 15m
      telemetry_gates:
        - name: p50-latency
          comparator: lt
          value_ms: 350
        - name: error-rate
          comparator: lt
          value_pct: 0.5
        - name: token-cost-variance
          comparator: lte
          value_pct: 10
    - name: ramp-5
      percent: 5
      duration: 30m
      telemetry_gates: [p50-latency, error-rate]
    - name: full
      percent: 100
      duration: 0m
      auto_promote: false
fallback_policy:
  - when: region-unavailable
    action: failover-to
    target_region_priority: [us-east-1, us-west-2]
  - when: cost-exceeds
    threshold_usd_per_hour: 15
    action: fallback-to
    prefer: smaller-quantized-variants

Schema notes (shape)
--------------------
- name, target: strings, unique name required.
- selectors: array of simple matchers (path_prefix, header, method). Keep evaluation O(1).
- variants: each variant defines id (ref to model catalog), optional runtime_profile (prebaked kernel+quant profiles), capacity_hint (inform pricing and autoscaler).
- region_policy: per-variant per-region max_weight is required for multi-region policies. Default to 0 if omitted.
- rollout: a list of steps. Steps must be strictly increasing in percent. duration allowed to be 0 for instant promotes. Steps can reference named telemetry gates.
- telemetry_gates: structured but expressed as lightweight checks (name, comparator, value, lookback).

Lightweight JSON Schema (pseudo)
--------------------------------
We keep this small; actual schema lives in control-plane repo as JSON Schema / OpenAPI. Validators should be runnable locally.
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["name","target","variants","rollout"],
  "properties": {
    "name": {"type":"string"},
    "target": {"type":"string"},
    "variants": {"type":"array"},
    "rollout": {"type":"object"}
  }
}

Validation checklist (pre-apply)
--------------------------------
- Schema validation: rwctl validate-manifest <file> -> must pass JSON Schema.
- Referent checks: every variant.id must exist in model catalog and be compatible with runtime_profile.
- Region reachability: all regions listed must be in our supported regions list.
- Weight invariants: sum of per-region weights for a target must not exceed 1.0 (enforce within small epsilon).
- Capacity check: variant.capacity_hint * expected_qps <= sum(region_capacity) OR warn.
- Conflicting selectors: ensure there is not an overlapping higher-priority policy that conflicts; if overlap exists, require explicit priority field.
- Dry-run compile: rwctl compile-manifest --dry-run => shows computed per-region weights and expected traffic split.
- Security review: manifest with broad header selectors (e.g., match all tenants) must add a security signoff tag if used in prod.

CLI quick commands
------------------
- Validate syntax and schema: rwctl validate-manifest policy.yaml
- Run referent checks (model + region): rwctl check-references policy.yaml --models --regions
- Dry compile and show plan: rwctl compile-manifest policy.yaml --output plan.json --dry-run
- Submit for rollout (creates PR-like review): rwctl submit-rollout policy.yaml --approvers @sre-team

Rollout mechanics and gating
----------------------------
Progressive-canary is the recommended default for any change that influences routing or model variants. Key rules:
- Every step has explicit telemetry gates. If a gate fails, the rollout must automatically abort and trigger rollback.
- Telemetry lookback window defaults to 5 minutes for canaries, 15 minutes for ramps, configurable per step.
- Minimum sample size rule: if request count during the lookback is below X (default 500 requests), treat gate as inconclusive and extend step (by step.duration up to 2x) rather than progressing. This avoids noisy auto-promotes on low volume tenants.
- Rollback triggers (examples): p50 latency increase > 30% over baseline AND absolute p50 exceeds 500ms, error-rate increase > 1.0% absolute, token cost > 15% delta for 10m.

Multi-region specifics
----------------------
- Region-aware weights: manifest author should provide per-region max_weight for each variant. The control plane computes actual per-region weight respecting regional capacity and cost signals.
- Failover chains: author should declare fallback target regions by priority. On region outage event (control-plane healthcheck), traffic is redistributed to next priority region respecting the max_weight constraints.
- Time-of-day capacity shifts: allow optional time_windows to favor regions during region-local business hours (helps match latency/cost to demand).
- Cross-region latency guard: if RTT to fallback region from majority of clients exceeds threshold, automatically reduce weight and prefer local variants.

Observability mapping
---------------------
Every rollout action must emit a standardized event that maps to metrics and logs:
- rollout.event.{start|step|promote|abort|rollback} with metadata: manifest_name, step_name, percent, actor, commit_id.
- Metrics to evaluate gates: request_count, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_rate_pct, tokens_consumed, cost_usd_hour.
- Alerting: when a gate fails and rollout aborts, page on-call SRE and create incident with automated dump of last 30m traces.

Safety checklist (pre-rollout review)
------------------------------------
- [ ] Schema validated locally (rwctl).
- [ ] All variant IDs exist in model catalog and have quant/profile compatibility.
- [ ] Canary gates defined for each step and map to real metrics.
- [ ] Minimum sample size configured or left as system default.
- [ ] Fallback regions prioritized and reachable.
- [ ] Costs estimate reviewed for high-traffic changes (PLAT-ops notified if > $1k/day).
- [ ] Security signoff for wide selectors (if matches > 1000 tenants).
- [ ] Linked PR created for change in control-plane and config reviewed by 2 approvers.
- [ ] Run smoke tests: synthetic workload targeting canary for 30m and verify core invariants.

Testing harness suggestions
--------------------------
- Unit-test the manifest serializer and validator in control-plane repo.
- End-to-end test: a job that enacts a staged canary in a test cluster with traffic generator that simulates regional latency and capacity. Failure modes should include partial outage and noisy errors.
- Chaos test: randomly kill region control-plane nodes and ensure failover triggers and respects fallback priorities.

Open questions / TODOs
---------------------
- How to express advanced weight math (dynamic weights that depend on capacity signals) without making manifests Turing-complete? Suggest: provide a named policy type (dynamic-capacity-scaler) defined elsewhere and referenced by variant.
- Should we allow nested rollout branches (different step sequences per-region)? Pros: fine-grained control. Cons: complexity explosion. Tentatively NO in v1.
- Define canonical telemetry gate library (names + comparators) in control-plane repo so manifests can reference by name.

References and links
--------------------
- control-plane RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Routing+Control+Plane+RFC
- model catalog contract: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Model+Catalog+API
- rwctl docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/rwctl+CLI
- Example PR implementing these checks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/402

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- Focus review on the gating logic and minimum sample size behaviour; both are common sources of flakiness.
- If you want a stricter default, change initial_step to 0.1% and require more conservative gates.

Author: Priya Nambiar (platform-engineering)
